messages.content:
You lightly clean a meeting transcript made of "Name: line" speaker turns.

Rules:
- Keep EVERY speaker turn, in order, with its "Name:" label exactly as written. Never merge, reorder or
  re-attribute turns. Never paraphrase what someone decided or committed to.
- Inside turns, remove filler words (um, uh, like, you know). Report them as ONE correction of kind "filler"
  whose original lists the removed words, comma-separated, and whose resolved is "".
- Remove turns or sentences that are pure small talk unrelated to the work. Report each as kind "digression".
- Apply explicit self-corrections ("X, no wait, Y" means Y) as kind "self_correction".
- Resolve every relative or partial date ("next Wednesday", "Monday", "the 20th", "December 1st") against the
  meeting date and calendar below. Report each as kind "date_resolution": original is the spoken phrase,
  resolved is "<weekday> <ISO date>", e.g. "Wednesday 2026-11-04". "Next <weekday>" means the first such
  weekday after the meeting date; a bare weekday means the next one after the meeting date; "the 20th" means
  the next 20th on or after the meeting date.
- In clean_text append the resolved ISO date in brackets after each date phrase, e.g. "by November 3rd [2026-11-03]".
- Do not invent anything.

Transcript (uploaded by Priya):

Priya: Okay, let's get going. This is the Pocket v1 planning sync. Three things to lock today: platform, launch date and payments.
Rahul: On platform, my strong vote is iOS only for v1. We're three engineers. Doing Android properly at the same time doubles QA and we'd ship something mediocre on both.
Ananya: Agreed from the design side. Our early users skew iPhone anyway, and I'd rather nail one set of onboarding flows.
Priya: Fine. Decision: v1 is iOS only. Android moves to v2.
Rahul: Good. Then launch date. If we freeze scope this week, the twentieth of November is realistic.
Priya: Let's commit to it. Public launch is November 20th.
Rahul: Payments next. Stripe is nicer to integrate, but most of our users pay with UPI, and Razorpay handles UPI natively with lower fees in India.
Priya: Then it's Razorpay, not Stripe, for payments. We can revisit Stripe if we go international.
Ananya: For my part, I'll have the onboarding screens done by November 3rd.
Rahul: I'll get a TestFlight build out to the beta group by November 10th.
Priya: And I'll write the landing page copy by November 6th. Okay, that's everything. Thanks, both.
